logline: A royal guard haunted by past trauma investigates a series of scholar murders in the Joseon court - only to uncover that the conspiracy is tied to King Sejong's secret project to create a new alphabet for his people.

renewal.note: Single-season limited series of 24 episodes, concluded December 22, 2011 on SBS. Won the Grand Prize at the 2012 Baeksang Arts Awards.

bollymeter.basis: Averaged 19.4% nationwide (AGB Nielsen) with a finale reaching 25.4%. Won the Grand Prize at the 2012 Baeksang Arts Awards - the Korean industry's highest television honour. Rare for a historical thriller to hold both critical and popular consensus at this level.

seasons.review_body: Tree with Deep Roots is one of the most critically decorated Korean dramas of the 2010s - a historical thriller that won the Grand Prize at the 2012 Baeksang Arts Awards and averaged 19.4% nationwide (AGB Nielsen) across its 24-episode run, with the finale reaching 25.4%. Writers Kim Young-hyun and Park Sang-yeon frame the invention of Hangul - the Korean alphabet - as a conspiracy thriller rather than a celebratory biopic, surrounding King Sejong's linguistic project with murders, shadow organisations, and a bodyguard (Jang Hyuk) whose personal trauma links him to the king's past. Han Suk-kyu's King Sejong is a genuinely complex figure: idealist and strategist in one body, capable of ruthlessness in service of an idea he believes will free his people. The result is a rare case of historical K-drama that takes its subject matter seriously as political philosophy rather than court romance backdrop.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere opens in media res with a scholar murder that immediately signals this is not a conventional sageuk. The investigation framework is established quickly, and Jang Hyuk's Kang Chae-yoon arrives carrying a vendetta whose origins are deliberately withheld - effective tension architecture for a 24-episode run.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The discovery of the first murdered scholar - the crime whose solution will eventually reveal a secret that reshapes Korean history.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 24
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves both the investigation and the decade-long personal conflict between Chae-yoon and the king. The 25.4% viewership for this episode reflected an audience that had stayed invested through 24 hours of dense political and personal stakes.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Sejong's revelation of the full scope of his plan - and Chae-yoon's understanding of what he was actually protecting.
